html:
SMTO-EXE-0201 — SMTO got a PDF result it couldn't trust

GUID: cbfe47ea-5ccb-5c52-89b1-15c8657a3764
Slug: pdf-invalid-response
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • The Gateway computer sent back a PDF result that didn't add up, so SMTO didn't accept it. Your original PDF was not changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Artifacts from this run and, if you named a save location, check that folder for a new PDF or image. Knowing what already exists avoids making a duplicate when you ask again.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check for updates. If this Gateway then offers Update to a newer version, select it when no tasks are running on it. A Gateway on a different version than SMTO can send results in a form SMTO doesn't accept.
  3. If you asked for many pages or large page images, ask for fewer at a time. A very large reply from the Gateway can go over the size SMTO accepts.

What success looks like

  • Asking again returns a normal result, and only the files you expect appear under Artifacts from this run.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep repeating a request that saves files until you've checked what is already there.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The PDF result or staged-output receipt from the Gateway failed validation (malformed or oversized data, wrong source/output counts, unexpected staged file names or mismatched output hashes).

What this means

  • PDF result validation rejected malformed/oversized data, invalid cancellation facts, inconsistent source/output counts, staged names or output hashes. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • PDF result validation rejected malformed/oversized data, invalid cancellation facts, inconsistent source/output counts, staged names or output hashes.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect structural receipt/source/output consistency and the original operation's publication state without assuming no write happened.

How to fix it

  • Compare Server and Gateway versions (Settings > Setup > Gateways) and update the Gateway if they differ; validate_response rejects replies over the 2 MB envelope, failures with an unknown error_kind, incomplete success receipts and outputs missing path/filename/mime_type/sha256/size, and PdfService._publish rejects mismatched staged names, hashes or source counts. Before issuing another write, check the run's artifact workspace and any explicit output_path for files from the original request.
  • Inspect the protocol defect and original outputs; reconcile possible publication before requesting another write.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the bounded PDF receipt and input, reduce the request if needed, and retry only after resolving the reported condition.

How to verify the fix

  • The original outcome is reconciled and the producer supplies a valid bounded receipt.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
